title: Predictive factors of persistence of ascites after TIPS implantation
summary: Liver cirrhosis is a major healthcare problem in Germany with a high mortality. The high mortality is caused by complications of liver cirrhosis which are due to the development of portal hypertension. The major complications of portal hypertension are variceal bleeding and the development of ascites with the need for diuretic treatment and recurrent large-volume paracenteses. Implantation of a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt is a safe and effective treatment of portal hypertension. Patients who received TIPS implantation due to refractory ascites show complete ascites clearance in 51% and partial clearance in 68% without the need for further paracenteses . However, the summary of randomized trails evaluating the efficacy of TIPS implantation for treatment refractory ascites showed that in 42% of patients, recurrence of ascites is observed after successful TIPS implantation. The aim of this study with several subprojects is to analyze predictive factors of persistence of ascites after TIPS implantation with a special focus on neurohumeral mechanisms, pressure changes and factors of primary and secondary hemostasis.
